prompt: A ranked feed spends most of its serving budget applying a heavy model to every candidate. Which change directly targets that cost?

options.text: Assume ranking is free because the timeline IDs came from Redis.
options.explanation: Cache lookup and model inference are different stages with different costs.

options.text: Estimate GPU count from single-request response time alone.
options.explanation: Batching, utilisation and parallelism mean response time alone does not establish throughput.

options.text: Use a cheaper stage to narrow candidates, then measure the total cost and quality of both stages.
options.explanation: Correct. It reduces expensive evaluations, while accounting for the first stage and relevant items it might discard.

options.text: Change to CPUs and assume the workload disappears.
options.explanation: Alternative hardware needs benchmarking; the model work still exists.

workedExample: Gather candidates, fetch features and score cheaply before applying the expensive model to a smaller set. Include both stages’ resource cost and evaluate recall: an item removed early cannot be recovered by later ranking. Cache or degrade where the product permits, while retaining current visibility checks.

link.title: Meta engineering: how machine learning powers News Feed ranking
